page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It has a large L3 cache of 480 MB and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8i.8xlarge demonstrates strong performance in CPU-intensive tasks. It achieves a top-tier rating in LLM text generation for small models (135M) at 357.67 tokens per second, alongside strong ratings in single-threaded gzip compression (34.25 GB/sec) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (227.98 GB/sec). Geekbench scores are also strong, with a single-core score of 2187.0 and a multi-core score of 18229.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 178.37 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.8xlarge offers high compute density and advanced vector/matrix acceleration without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPUs. However, the lack of local NVMe SSDs represents a tradeoff for I/O-heavy workloads that require ultra-low latency storage. The instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as web serving, software compilation, single-node machine learning inference for small-to-medium models, and CPU-bound data processing.
